findings.title: Team admins who are not owners are denied access
findings.body: This requires the caller to satisfy both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`. Team admins and team owners are distinct roles, so an admin who is not also an owner cannot add guests even though the permission check and UI are intended to allow either role. Use an OR between these role checks.

findings.title: Guest deduplication is case-sensitive
findings.body: Email addresses are compared verbatim against existing attendees and blacklist entries. Since email addresses are case-insensitive in normal use, submitting a different-case version of an existing attendee or blacklisted address can bypass these checks. This can create duplicate attendees or evade the blacklist; normalize both inputs and stored addresses before comparison.

findings.title: Concurrent requests can add the same guest twice
findings.body: The handler filters against the attendees loaded before the write, then inserts the filtered list without an atomic duplicate check. Two requests adding the same email concurrently can both pass this check and create duplicate attendees (and send duplicate invitations). Enforce uniqueness in the database or make the insert idempotent.

findings.title: Guests can be added to cancelled bookings
findings.body: The handler never checks the booking status before inserting attendees and sending invitations. A permitted user can add guests to a cancelled booking, resulting in new attendees receiving a scheduled-event invitation for an event that no longer exists. Reject cancelled or otherwise ineligible bookings before modifying attendees.

findings.title: Guest list has no size limit
findings.body: The input accepts an unbounded number of email addresses. An authenticated user permitted to add guests can submit a very large list, causing bulk database writes, calendar updates, and one or more emails per attendee. Add a reasonable maximum (and enforce it server-side) to prevent resource exhaustion.
